title: “The king of Sheshach shall drink after them” — who or what is Sheshach?
summary: Jeremiah 25:26 ends the list of those who drink the cup with “the king of Sheshach shall drink after them”, and 51:41 says “How is Sheshach taken!” beside “Babylon”. The verses quoted do not say what Sheshach is.
text: KJV Jeremiah 25:26: “And all the kings of the north, far and near, one with another, and all the kingdoms of the world, which are upon the face of the earth: and the king of Sheshach shall drink after them.” KJV Jeremiah 51:41: “How is Sheshach taken! and how is the praise of the whole earth surprised! how is Babylon become an astonishment among the nations!” A whole-word, case-sensitive search of the packaged KJV for “Sheshach” returns these two verses only.
reasoning: Sheshach is named twice in the packaged KJV and is not explained in either verse. In 51:41 the name sits in a line with “the praise of the whole earth” and with “Babylon”, but the verse does not say that the two names are one. In 25:26 it is the last in a list of kingdoms and has “the king” of it. Possible readings: another name for Babylon; the name of a different place or people. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the two verses quoted and a word search of the packaged KJV for the name. The record does not say that any reading is the right one, does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek, and does not examine other books.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: the king of Sheshach shall drink after them

title: “Neither shall they visit it; neither shall that be done any more” — what is said to become of the ark of the covenant in Jeremiah 3:16?
summary: Jeremiah 3:16 says that in “those days” they shall say no more “The ark of the covenant of the Lord”, and that “neither shall it come to mind”. The verse does not say why, or what has become of the ark.
text: KJV Jeremiah 3:16: “And it shall come to pass, when ye be multiplied and increased in the land, in those days, saith the Lord, they shall say no more, The ark of the covenant of the Lord: neither shall it come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they visit it; neither shall that be done any more.” KJV 2 Chronicles 35:3: “And said unto the Levites that taught all Israel, which were holy unto the Lord, Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Israel did build; it shall not be a burden upon your shoulders: serve now the Lord your God, and his people Israel,”
reasoning: The verse says what will no longer be said, thought of, remembered, visited or done, and puts it in the future, in the days when the people are “multiplied and increased in the land”. It does not say whether the ark is then gone, kept, or replaced. “Neither shall that be done any more” does not say what “that” is: making the ark, visiting it, or the saying. 2 Chronicles 35:3 puts the ark “in the house which Solomon … did build”. Possible readings: the ark is lost or taken; the ark is set aside in favour of Jerusalem as the throne of the Lord (the verse that follows); the saying is only dropped. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the two verses quoted. The record does not say that any reading is the right one, does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek, and does not claim that no other passage says more about the ark.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: neither shall it come to mind: neither shall they remember it; neither shall they visit it; neither shall that be done any more

title: “These nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years” — from what event are the seventy years counted?
summary: Jeremiah 25:11 says the nations “shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years” and 29:10 says “after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you”. The verses quoted do not say what event begins the count.
text: KJV Jeremiah 25:11: “And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.” KJV Jeremiah 25:12: “And it shall come to pass, when seventy years are accomplished, that I will punish the king of Babylon, and that nation, saith the Lord, for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans, and will make it perpetual desolations.” KJV Jeremiah 29:10: “For thus saith the Lord, That after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place.” KJV 2 Chronicles 36:21: “To fulfil the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years.”
reasoning: Jeremiah 25:11 gives a length of time and a service, and 25:12 says what happens “when seventy years are accomplished”. Jeremiah 29:10 puts the seventy years “at Babylon” and says what follows them for the people addressed. None of the three verses names the year or event from which the seventy are counted, and 25:11 speaks of “these nations” serving while 29:10 speaks of a visit to those in Babylon. 2 Chronicles 36:21 says the land lay desolate “to fulfil threescore and ten years”. Possible readings: from the first carrying away; from the fall of Jerusalem and the burning of the temple; from the start of Babylon’s rule over the nations. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the verses quoted. The record does not say that any reading is the right one, does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek, and does not examine other books that mention the seventy years.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years
